title: nvme: Expand NVMe/NVMe-MI decode and dissect Security payloads
description:
## What this does

* Adds NVMe and NVMe-MI dissectors,
* new payload path for NVMe Admin Security Send/Receive with a TCG Storage dissector behind it,
* transport-level fixes in MCTP, MCTP-over-SMBus and NVMe/TCP.\*

### NVMe / NVMe-MI decode

NVMe Base 2.3 and NVMe-MI 2.1:

- **Identify.** Identify Controller and Identify Namespace grew the fields NVMe 2.x defines in what NVMe 1.4 left Reserved (see below), and the I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace (CNS 08h) is decoded for the first time. LBA Format handling now accounts for NULBAF, not just NLBAF.
- **Log pages.** Error Information, SMART/Health, telemetry, firmware slot, device self-test, sanitize status, endurance group, ANA, LBA Status, reservation notification and the supported-commands pages were extended; add Physical Interface Receiver Eye Opening Measurement (LID 19h).
- **Features.** Set Features and the matching Get Features CQE dword 0 decode, including the transfer structures (Timestamp, APST, Host Behavior Support, PLM Config, LBA Range Type).
- **NVMe-MI.** The Admin command set (prohibited-opcode list completed against NVMe-MI 2.1's "List of NVMe Admin Commands Supported using the Out-of-Band Mechanism", DOFST/DLEN validation) and the MI command set (Asynchronous Event configuration on Configuration Set, the AE Supported List on Configuration Get, the NSHDS Status Warning bitmask, CIAP in the message header). The Optionally/MEB Supported Command List's Opcode entries are now named from the correct table for each entry's own NMIMT (MI vs Admin) instead of rendering as a bare byte, and the Configuration Identifier field's Reserved/Vendor Specific bands are named in the tree the same way the packet list already synthesized them.

### Security Send/Receive and TCG Storage

- A new dissector table, **`nvme.security.secp`**, keyed on the Security Protocol field, with `struct nvme_security_info` (SECP, SPSP, direction) as the data pointer.
- SECP 00h (Security Protocol Information) is decoded natively.
- **`packet-tcg-storage.c`** registers against the table for SECP 01h and 02h and decodes ComPacket/Packet/Subpacket framing, the token-atom stream (tiny/short/medium/long atoms, UIDs, control tokens), Level 0 Discovery with its feature descriptors, method status codes and ComID management (TCG Storage Architecture Core 2.01, SIIS).

Dispatch is deliberately conservative: a payload is handed on only when the window starts at offset 0 and is not known to be short. A Security Send whose payload is smaller than its Dword 11 Transfer Length is a partial transfer and stays a byte blob; a Security Receive is always dispatched, since its Allocation Length is only an upper bound and a short payload there may well be a complete response.

### Transports

- **MCTP**: reassembly is keyed on the message tag _and_ the tag-owner bit (see fix 11 below), and the DSP0239 message-type set is labelled in full (SPDM, Secured Messages, CXL FM/CCI, PCIe-MI, the two vendor-defined types).
- **MCTP over SMBus**: PEC verification, and the expanded decode around it.
- **NVMe/TCP**: discovery log page, command-set and log-page decode picked up the shared NVMe changes; Termination Request PDUs are length-checked.

## Bug fixes

None of these are regressions from this work — they are defects in the code this commit touches.

### Values decoded incorrectly

|  | defect | effect |
|--|--------|--------|
| 1 | `post_add_bytes_from_16bytes()` called `tvb_get_uint64(tvb, off, 0)` and `tvb_get_uint64(tvb, off, 8)` — the third argument is the _encoding_, not an offset | the high 64 bits were a second big-endian read of the low 8 bytes; every 128-bit SMART counter rendered a wrong number |
| 2 | `post_add_intval_from_16bytes()` read both halves big-endian | same fields, wrong byte order (NVMe is little-endian) |
| 3 | Identify Controller FGUID (VSEI/OUI/EI) read little-endian | FGUID is a byte string, displayed reversed |
| 4 | Firmware Slot log page revisions decoded as `FT_UINT64` hex | FRS is eight ASCII characters per slot; now rendered as text |
| 5 | Error Information log page: bytes 42–65 rendered as one 24-byte Reserved run | hid the Command Set Indicator, Opcode and Log Page Version fields; the run is 21 bytes |
| 6 | Error Information decode bailed out at `off > 42` | over NVMe-MI, every window past byte 42 rendered nothing |
| 7 | NVMe-MI MIC computed and displayed byte-swapped (two cancelling swaps) | `nvme-mi.mic` did not match the value the endpoint computed |
| 8 | MCTP-over-SMBus put the PEC at the last byte of the frame | DSP0237 §6.3 fixes it immediately after the last data byte; with trailing bytes present those are different bytes. The PEC is now also verified (SMBus 3.3 CRC-8, computed locally — neither in-tree CRC-8 helper implements that variant) |
| 9 | MCTP-over-SMBus handed the trailing bytes to the data dissector starting _at_ the PEC | the PEC was re-rendered as trailing data and the last trailing byte was dropped |
| 10 | NVMe/TCP read HLEN and PDO with `tvb_get_int8()` | sign-extended for values ≥ 80h |
| 11 | MCTP reassembly keyed on the 3-bit message tag alone (`fst & 0x7`) | DSP0236 identifies a message by source EID, tag owner **and** message tag, and tags are tracked independently per TO value; a request (TO=1) and its response (TO=0) reusing the same tag value collided on one reassembly id. The key is now the low nibble, TO included — the same value `pinfo->srcport`/`destport` already used |
| 12 | `add_ctrl_lblocks()` and the microsecond formatter passed `"%s"` as a _value_ to `snprintf` | the label printed a literal `%s` |
| 13 | Identify CNS read as a 16-bit field | CNS is CDW10 07:00; byte 41 is Reserved, so a nonzero Reserved byte misdispatched the response decode |

### Wrong masks, labels and types

|  | defect |
|--|--------|
| 14 | HCTM Thermal Management Temperatures 1 and 2 had **no mask at all** — both read the whole dword (Set Features and the Get Features CQE) |
| 15 | Error Information Parameter Error Location: `bite` masked 0x7ff, `rsvd` masked 0xf8ff — overlapping and wrong |
| 16 | Discovery log page TREQ: `secch` was `FT_BOOLEAN`/0x1, but NVMe 2.x makes it a two-bit enum; `sqfc` sat at 0x2 instead of 0x4 |
| 17 | Get Log Page LSP masked 5 bits (0x1f00), spec says 7; UUID Index masked 0x3f, spec says 0x7f |
| 18 | SMART Critical Warning was missing the Indeterminate Personality State bit, and its Reserved mask covered it |
| 19 | Bitmask _group containers_ carried a subfield's mask (`ana.grp.anas` 0xf, `prop_get_set.attrib` 0x7) |
| 20 | Several Reserved fields masked more than the dword's Reserved range (Identify CDW11, Get Log Page CDW14, Power Management, Temperature Threshold, APST ITPT) |
| 21 | 32 fields carried the wrong display name — four Error Information fields all read "Namespace ID", a Reserved field read "Work Hint", six read "DWORD0"/"DWORD11"/"DWORD12", RATYPE read "Number of LBA Range Descriptors", plus typos ("Dorbell", "most resent", "Itra-host", "I/0 Command Supported"). Filter names are unchanged for all of these except where noted below |
| 22 | Interrupt Vector Configuration (FID 09h): `iv` had no mask at all (rendered the whole CDW11/CQE DW0), and `cd` was a boolean over a 17-bit mask covering `iv` too, so it read "set" whenever any interrupt vector bit was nonzero |

### Reserved-run drift

The largest group. Reserved runs written against NVMe 1.4 cover fields NVMe 2.0 and later define, so live data rendered as padding: Identify Controller (five separate runs, including the NVMe-oF one at byte 1806), Identify Namespace (bytes 31–103 went entirely undecoded, plus the LBA Format region), and the Error Information, SMART and Endurance Group log pages. Each run was re-cut against NVMe Base 2.3 and the newly exposed fields decoded.

### NVMe-MI response layout and lifecycle

- **Control Primitive error responses** were decoded with the Success body layout. NVMe-MI 2.1 makes the response body format depend on the Status field, so an Abort failure invented a Tag (a false mismatch against the request) and a CPSR, from which the decode fabricated a CPAS. The shared error-response helper now owns those bytes, as it already does on the MI and Admin paths.
- **A sliced frame threw while computing its MIC** before the command slot was claimed, so the request never took the slot and the next response linked to the wrong frame — a wrong Request In and a wrong Response Time on a frame that looks healthy. The MIC computation is now guarded, and a frame whose covered bytes are not all present reports the MIC as unverified rather than asserting a verdict the capture cannot support.
- **A data window that no structured decoder rendered** had its raw-bytes item hidden anyway, because the dispatcher returned "handled" on the opcode alone. A 64-byte window is normal at a 2-Wire MTU, so this hid the payload for a BMC walking a 4,096-byte structure. The choice is now made on what actually landed in the subtree.
- **The AE list header length** was assumed to be 5 bytes rather than read from the header's own AEELHL/AESLHL field.

### NVMe/TCP

- A Termination Request PDU with PLEN below its own 24-byte header underflowed the trailing-data length; `tcp_dissect_pdus()` only guarantees PLEN ≥ the 8-byte common header. Now reported as malformed.

## Expert info

`packet-nvme.c` 

| condition | severity |
|-----------|----------|
| completion Status Code or Status Code Type nonzero | Note |
| NLBAF + NULBAF exceed the LBA Format list the structure holds | Warn |
| transport declared more data than the frame carries | Warn |
| log page window does not start on a record boundary | Warn |
| Number of Descriptors exceeds what the response holds | Warn |


Elsewhere: NVMe-MI adds `nvme-mi.mic_unverified`, `nvme-mi.admin.invalid_dofst` and `nvme-mi.admin.invalid_dlen`; MCTP-over-SMBus adds `mctp.smbus.pec_bad`; NVMe/TCP adds `nvme-tcp.termreq_too_short`; TCG Storage ships five of its own.

## Testing

New and extended dissection suites, all driven by synthetic captures generated from checked-in generators (`tools/gen-nvme-mi-test-capture.py`, `tools/gen-nvme-tcp-test-capture.py`, `tools/gen-mctp-smbus-test-capture.py`):

| suite | tests |
|-------|-------|
| `suite_dissection_nvme.py` | 4 -\> 25 |
| `suite_dissection_nvme_mi.py` | 225 -\> 326 |
| `suite_dissection_mctp_smbus.py` | 31 -\> 44 |
| `suite_dissection_tcg_storage.py` | new, 42 |

Nine new captures cover the Eye Opening Measurement log page, the Security/TCG payload path, NVMe-MI error paths, TCG atom classes and malformed token streams, NVMe/TCP discovery, command sets, a windowed log page and a truncated PDU. Existing captures regenerate byte-identically from the updated generators.

Ran Fuzzing 20 threads 9 hours over the relevant captures.

## Note on spec citations

Comments cite spec figures by **title** rather than by number ("the NVMe-MI Message Fields figure", not "Figure 12"). Figure numbering shifts between revisions of these specs, so a number that is right for NVMe-MI 2.1 misleads a reader holding 2.0 or a later revision; the titles are stable. Existing citations in the touched files were converted for consistency.

nvme: Expand NVMe/NVMe-MI decode and dissect Security payloads

Add additional NVMe Base 2.3 and NVMe-MI 2.1 dissection:
Identify Controller and Namespace (including I/O Command Set Independent
Identify Namespace, CNS 08h), the Error Information, SMART, telemetry,
firmware slot, self-test, sanitize, endurance group and eye opening
measurement log pages, Set/Get Features, and the NVMe-MI Admin and MI
command sets.

Fix some existing NVMe and NVMe-MI dissection issues.

Add the "nvme.security.secp" dissector table, route NVMe Admin Security
Send and Security Receive payloads to it, and decode SECP 00h directly.
Add packet-tcg-storage.c, registers and decodes TCG Storage payloads:
ComPacket/Packet/Subpacket framing, token atoms, Level 0 Discovery,
